doc.title: Peter Appleyard interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, October 4, 2012

title: Getting hired by Frank Sinatra without an audition
summary: Irv Cottler told him Sinatra wanted vibes, and Appleyard got the two-week run without an audition.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working with Sinatra: bands, Vegas and the Sands

blocks.x: Maybe he learned that from Benny Goodman.

And then, Whilst I was with Benny, in New York, Mr. Sinatra was going to have a show for two weeks at the Eros Theater with Ella Fitzgerald and the Basie Band, and a huge string section. And I went down to buy tickets and I couldn’t get any, they were sold out. So I went over to Manny’s Music Shop and I ran into Irv Cottler, his drummer.

Yeah. A very good drummer, he was with Frank all those great years. And he said, “Peter, how are you?” I said, “Fine, Irv, how are you?” He said, “Good.” He said, “We were talking about you last night.” I said, “Who, me? Who?” He said, “Bill Miller,” pianist, “and Frank and me.” I said, “What are you talking about me for?” He said, “Well Frank wants to use vibes at the Eros, and Bill Miller said, “‘Well why don’t we get Peter Appleyard?’” So Frank said, “Peter Appleyard?” He said, “Yeah.” He said, “He works with Benny.” He said, “If he works with Benny, get him.” I got the job without an audition.
I guess you solved that problem of not being able to get tickets to the show.
My wife came down and sat in the — no one else could sit in the audience, just one person, and she sat there to hear Frank rehearse with us.

At the end of the run — oh, on the second day he came up to me and he said, “Peter, I owe you an apology.” I said, “What?” Frank Sinatra. I said, “What for?” He said, “There’s not enough here to play.” He said, “But sweetheart if you feel like playing behind me or Ella do it.” At the end of the run he gives a party like it wouldn’t quit on stage with him, the most beautiful wine and Italian food. He gave me a sterling silver jewelry box, engraved, “Peter, thanks F.S.” He was a great guy. Generous, generous man.
